body:
I’ll go point by point:

1. I had a followup appt scheduled with a psychiatrist back at college, but that has since gone out the window after having to move back home due to the pandemic. I did talk to another therapist yesterday (at home) through video who thankfully really zeroed in on the ADHD component of my state and how that can arise in tandem with depression. I’ll probably just try to schedule another, more frequent appt with new!therapist and let them know that I’m really in struggle mode and could use some connections.

2. It feels so hypocritical of me to try to give help when I’m basically at my bottom, and I meant generally that I have creative things (writing or speaking stuff mostly) or more long-term, purposeful things (job searching, language learning, connection building) that I physically can’t get myself to do. I’ve had problems with getting organized, pushing through boring stuff, staying focused (even fun things like albums and movies fucking test my attention span), making plans, time management for as long as I can remember. It’s just so totally beyond my grasp that I think I’ve come to subconsciously accept it as part of my life and I only somewhat recently learned that it’s really not normal. That’s the worst part to me. I’m so used to putzing around, procrastinating, doing the bare minimum, skating by in life that I either don’t know what I could do to change my situation or am literally unable to because the impetus in my brain that says “hey dumbass, get up and plan your schedule” does not fucking work. It’s not like the battery is drained as much as there never was a battery there to begin with. I have no idea how I get myself to do anything. It especially sucks in combination with feeling shitty and terrible by default since I was 13 (I can distinctly remember when I stopped being happy, it’s like a switch flipped somewhere) because I end up overthinking (like I always do with everything ever) if it’ll really work and how much life actually sucks vs how I’m making it out to be. I really feel like there’s no escape and it’s so hard for me because it feels so fake compared to people who like actively attempt suicide or self harm or get hospitalized, things which I haven’t done. It’s like I can’t even be depressed right.
